programme.sub-title: Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress E01 [English Subtitle]
programme.desc: At a time when the industrial revolution was carrying the world into the modern age, a horde of undead monsters suddenly appeared. They could not be killed unless their hearts, which were protected by a layer of iron, were pierced. Humans bitten by them would come back as undead monsters themselves. These undead, which would later be known as "Kabane," exploded in population until they finally overran the world. The people of Hinomoto, a nation in the far east, built fortresses known as "stations" throughout the land that have allowed them to survive the threat of the Kabane. People can only travel between these stations using fortified steam locomotives known as "Hayajiro," and they have managed to stay alive by sharing resources in this way. Ikoma is a young steamsmith living at Aragane Station, a city that specializes in the manufacture of iron and steam engines. He is working on developing a unique anti-Kabane weapon called a "piercing gun" as he waits for his chance to prove his strength. Then, one day, a Hayajiro called the "Iron Fortress" makes its way through the front lines to arrive at Aragane Station. When Ikoma begins his usual maintenance routine, he sees a mysterious girl who is exempt from her Kabane inspection. That night, Ikoma sees the girl again and learns that her name is Mumei, but then an out-of-control Hayajiro overrun by Kabane charges into Aragane Station. The Kabane pour out of the train into Aragane Station. Ikoma races against the flow of the panicked residents, this time determined not to run away, but to defeat the Kabane with his piercing gun!

programme.title: Girls Band Cry

programme.title: Girls Band Cry

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: Subaru's grandmother unexpectedly visits Tokyo. Subaru wants to pursue music, not acting, but when she tries to tell her grandmother, she puts on a fake smile and plays the role of the good granddaughter instead.

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: A live house where Momoka used to play asks the girls to perform, and they agree to enter their first battle of the bands. As they struggle to meet the ticket sales quota, Momoka gets tickets to a show by her former band.

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: The three girls practice to improve as a band. Nina is obsessed with beating Diamond Dust and researches ways to boost their popularity, but finds nothing useful. Tomo and Rupa then approach Nina after seeing the three girls perform.

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: Tomo and Rupa join Nina, Subaru, and Momoka, forming a five-member band. Momoka finds an upcoming show, but their different personalities clash. Nina and Momoka have different views of the band as they take the stage with their relationship strained.

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: After the live show, Nina and Momoka's fight intensifies. Nina gives up her escape routes to pursue music professionally. Tomo threatens to quit if their rocky relationship continues. On Nina's first day at work, Momoka shows up.

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: Traumatized by past experiences, Tomo struggles to express her feelings to the band. When Nina asks for feedback on her guitar playing, Tomo is harsh, but seeing Nina refuse to give up gives Tomo the confidence to change.

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: Nina's parents visit from her hometown as she dedicates herself to the band. After running away, Nina reluctantly returns home. She tries to talk to her father, but he fails to understand her perspective. The next day, he takes her to her old high school.

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: At a massive outdoor music festival, Nina and the band are fired up by the huge stage. Diamond Dust has grown stronger, but Nina refuses to lose. Determined to leave their mark, the band begins the performance of a lifetime.

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: After signing with a talent agency, Nina and the band are challenged by Diamond Dust, who now have twice their followers. Split on whether to accept, they face the battle with low ticket sales—but take the stage and stay true to themselves.

programme.title: Girls Band Cry
programme.desc: Nina's band falls far behind Diamond Dust in ticket sales for the battle of the bands, facing the harsh reality of their competition. Despite this, Nina and the band stay true to themselves and take the stage to play their song.

programme.title: CBS News Sunday Morning
programme.desc: The sparkling notes of a trumpet fanfare and the familiar logo of the sun alert viewers that it's time for CBS's Sunday morning staple. Journalist Jane Pauley helms the show, taking over hosting duties from Charles Osgood, who spent 22 years on the job. A morning talk show, this program airs at a different pace and focuses much of its attention on the performing arts. After a quick update of the day's news and national weather, correspondents offer longer-length segments on a variety of topics, from architecture to ballet to music to pop culture to politics.

programme.title: RAZOR: The Future of Fishing
programme.desc: The Earth will be home to nearly 10 billion people by 2050, and we need to figure out a sustainable way to feed them all. One solution could be fish farming. Seafood is already responsible for 17 percent of the world's protein intake, and aquaculture is the fastest growing food supply sector in the world. RAZOR's Reya El-Salahi travels to the Arctic Circle, in Norway, where the company Salten Smolt is farming salmon on land while recycling up to 90 percent of its water. It uses a technology called Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS), which is also being tested by Nord University on warm water fish like tilapia. Salten Smolt says the future of sustainable fish farming is both in tanks on land and technologically-advanced open water pens. Meanwhile on the island of Indre Haroya, the company Salmon Evolution is growing fish in tanks until harvest, using a Hybrid Flow-Through System (HFS) that recycles up to 65 % of the seawater it takes from the ocean. Salmon Evolution says that's a sweet spot that balances both sustainability and costs.

programme.title: RAZOR: Rewilding Bison
programme.desc: Once widespread across Europe, the European bison was driven to extinction in the wild by overhunting. Now, thanks to decades of conservation and reintroduction efforts, the species is making a comeback. In Romania's Tarcu Mountains, bison have returned after more than 200 years, with over 120 now roaming freely. RAZOR's Emma Keeling treks through the mountains to meet the team behind the rewilding project, jointly led by WWF and Rewilding Europe. The return of bison is benefiting more than 600 other species, from microorganisms to large carnivores, while creating new opportunities for local communities through ecotourism. How can bringing a species back from the brink help restore an entire ecosystem and build a more sustainable relationship between people and nature?

programme.title: China's Economy and the World: Exploring the 15th Five-Year Plan and global economic order shift
programme.desc: In this special series, "China's Economy and the World," expert Sławomir Majman, Vice President of the Polish Institute of Security and International Development and former President of the Polish Information and Foreign Investment Agency, explores China's 15th Five-Year Plan and the reshaping global economic order.

programme.title: Architecture Intelligence: The Mission
programme.desc: An all-new documentary series and a true gift for engineering enthusiasts. Join CGTN's Yang Zhao on a captivating global journey, exploring a league of ambitious new engineering marvels. Uncover the extraordinary challenges and ingenious strategies behind these colossal structures. CGTN's award-winning Tech It Out studio embraces the popular short video format to innovate a brand-new style of engineering documentary and present "Architecture Intelligence," a nine-episode series. With our host Yang Zhao, we travel around the world and go beyond just witnessing mega-structures; we delve into the soul of each place we visit. We place architecture within the context of human lives, allowing it to serve as a lens through which we gain insights into a city, a nation and its culture.

programme.title: Innovation Has Its Way, Warmth Knows No Bounds
programme.desc: Have you ever seen a gala where robots take center stage? In Shanghai, a “Robot Gala” puts Chinese-made humanoid robots front and center — dancing, greeting customers, and even helping in classrooms. AI companions, from plush toys to holograms, are reshaping emotional connection in urban life. In Beijing, personalized tours led by multilingual guides help global travelers discover the Forbidden City and beyond. And in Thailand’s sugarcane fields, Chinese agricultural machinery is solving a labor crisis for local farmers. From cutting-edge technology to warm companionship, from cultural export to agricultural assistance, this episode of Meet China takes you to see how Chinese innovation unlocks a new picture of technology empowering life and cooperation promoting development.

programme.title: Dubai Chambers chairman: Chinese innovation is very welcome in Dubai
programme.desc: Dubai is already home to over 6,600 Chinese companies, but the emirate wants to see more. Sultan bin Saeed Al Mansoori, chairman of Dubai Chambers, said in an interview with CGTN that Dubai welcomes innovation and creativity from China and is open to more partnerships and cooperation.

programme.title: Live: Finding smart care and rehab solutions at 140th Canton Fair
programme.desc: The 140th China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, is underway in Guangzhou, south China, showcasing high-tech care and rehabilitation devices, from exoskeletons to stair-climbing wheelchairs. Millions of people worldwide need care and rehabilitation, and many can't afford it or reach it. CGTN's Zheng Songwu visits the fair's dedicated zone to test the latest devices and speak with international buyers about how China is helping meet that demand.

programme.title: Live: Canton Fair's 'hidden champions' - small firms, global reach
programme.desc: They're not household names, but global supply chains depend on them. At the 140th Canton Fair, CGTN reporter He Jingyi joins Johann Anton Klimmer, managing director of the Rothenberger Group and a longtime Canton Fair buyer, to explore specialized sectors - from hardware and tools to precision components, general machinery, and lighting and electrical products. These specialized SMEs are the backbone of China's manufacturing sector - and help keep global production moving. What can seemingly ordinary products tell us about the strength of a much larger industry?

programme.title: 140th Canton Fair - machines built to work with humans
programme.desc: Seventy years ago, the Canton Fair featured Chinese tea, silk and handmade goods. Today, it's about robots. Join us to see dexterous robotic hands, exoskeletons and companion robots, and how AI works alongside humans.

programme.title: Xinjiang's role in Eurasia connectivity
programme.desc: From the bustling lanes of the world's largest bazaar in Urumqi to the humming logistics hubs at the region's 19 ports, Xinjiang is transforming its geographical advantage into economic strength. As China's gateway to the west, it now hosts a major network for opening-up, including the pioneering Pilot Free Trade Zone. This episode explores how cross-border trade, a web of China-Europe freight trains, and cultural exchanges are weaving Xinjiang into the very heart of the Belt and Road Initiative, making it a pivotal hub for continental connectivity.

programme.title: China Agenda 2026
programme.desc: Special coverage of China's annual sessions of its top legislature and political advisory body, known as the "Two Sessions".

programme.title: Inside China's Q3 Economy
programme.desc: China's economy expanded 4.6% in the first three quarters, with exports and high-tech manufacturing continuing to provide support, while consumption and industrial output picked up in September. What do the latest numbers reveal about China's growth momentum and economic transformation? Can renewed momentum and an improved structure help sustain growth in the months ahead? Join BizTalk as leading economists and experts take a closer look at China's Q3 economic performance, unpack the key signals behind the headline numbers, and assess the outlook for growth.

programme.title: Adidas CEO: Competition with Chinese brands makes us better
programme.desc: German sportswear giant Adidas has been in China for decades, but it's no longer just selling a European playbook. Its "In China, For China" model puts designers, creatives and supply chains directly into the bustle of the world's second largest economy - where competition is fierce and Chinese sportswear brands are stronger than ever. Recently in Shanghai, CGTN reporter Wang Tianyu caught up with Adidas global CEO Bjørn Gulden to find out more.

programme.title: Xinjiang's role in Eurasia connectivity
programme.desc: From the bustling lanes of the world's largest bazaar in Urumqi to the humming logistics hubs at the region's 19 ports, Xinjiang is transforming its geographical advantage into economic strength. As China's gateway to the west, it now hosts a major network for opening-up, including the pioneering Pilot Free Trade Zone. This episode explores how cross-border trade, a web of China-Europe freight trains, and cultural exchanges are weaving Xinjiang into the very heart of the Belt and Road Initiative, making it a pivotal hub for continental connectivity.

programme.title: How China's ocean kingdom makes billions
programme.desc: In Southern China, a theme park you've likely never heard of is attracting more annual visitors than Hollywood Universal. The question is, how? Meet Chimelong Ocean Kingdom. It holds seven Guinness World Records and features the largest aquarium on earth. CGTN's Yu Hongyu dives into the strategy behind the splash to see how a local park created a hundred-billion-dollar opportunity.

programme.title: China's Kungfu theme park: A wild ride back in time
programme.desc: At Wansuishan Martial Arts City in central China’s Kaifeng, Henan Province, you’re not just a visitor - you’re part of the story. Every segment in the park is part of an immersive experience rooted in Chinese martial arts and traditional culture. From live matchmaking shows to iron flower performances, from Song Dynasty streets to interactive stages, this uniquely Chinese theme park – with not even one roller coaster or scary ride – was able to record over 24 million visits in 2025.

programme.title: Bizfocus: From myth to reality: How tech brings Eastern imagination to life
programme.desc: Ever wondered what China’s version of “Adam and Eve” or “Beauty and the Beast” looks like? While the world’s theme parks are all about Western fairy tales, one Chinese park took a different path—Fantawild brings ancient Eastern myths to life with mind-blowing tech and art. In this episode of Bizfocus, CGTN’s Xu Yi and her new friends from Pakistan and Bangladesh go for adventure in Fantawild Oriental Heritage in Mianyang, Sichuan. Gods, legends, and the tech behind the magic—all in one epic trip.

programme.title: China Bound: Chongqing
programme.desc: Join us in southwest China's Chongqing, one of the world's biggest cities. From futuristic skylines and cyberpunk streets, to fire-breathing opera, spicy hotpot and kungfu tea, we're diving deep into this megacity the size of Austria.

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China. In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui Museum, show the amazing giant bronze mask, exquisite gold stuff, marvelous bronze divine tree etc., re-explore this mysterious and great civilization 3000 years ago.

programme.title: Crunch and Munch in Macao Ep.3
programme.desc: Feast on the stories behind Macao's iconic dishes and its people - One Country, Two Systems, endless flavors.

programme.title: Chengdu Lacquerware Art
programme.desc: Chengdu lacquerware is unique, thanks to its "three carvings and one engraving" technique. Along with its bold decorative style, this has made it a gem of Chinese lacquer art. Chengdu lacquerware also emphasizes the use of vibrant colors. Pieces are brought to beautiful life by bright red, vivid yellow, emerald green, and other striking hues.

programme.title: Discovering the Ancient Grottoes of Chongqing
programme.desc: The third episode of the Chongqing Series, Humanistic Chongqing, focuses on the Dazu Stone Carvings in Chongqing. In 1999, the Dazu Stone Carvings were inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List. As an outstanding representative of China's late grotto carving art, they integrate the essence of Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism in their content, fully embodying the beauty of cultural integration. This episode comprehensively showcases the profound historical and cultural heritage of Dazu and its vibrant contemporary folk customs, exploring the thematic connotations, artistic characteristics and historical origins of the Dazu Stone Carvings, as well as their far-reaching influence on the local people for generations.

programme.title: China's Extraordinary Hotels 3 - Living Large
programme.desc: The third episode of the China's Extraordinary Hotels Series introduces three domestic high-end hotels with each private brand: 1. Diaoyutai Hotel Hangzhou; 2. HuaQing Palace Hotel and Spa Xi'an; 3. Songtsam Linka Shangri-la Hotel. It highlights not only the hotels' surroundings, architectural styles and interior furnishings, but also their exclusive brand visions and management philosophies.

programme.title: Hanggai brings Inner Mongolian grasslands to New York
programme.desc: You don't need to speak the language to be captivated by Hanggai's music. This Chinese folk-rock band blends powerful vocals, traditional instruments and rock energy into a sound all its own. This summer, Hanggai returns to Lincoln center, bringing the beautiful melodies of the Inner Mongolian Steppe to New York. The band members share their expectations, and the stories behind their music.

programme.title: Foodwise: How to Order Chinese Food
programme.desc: How do you order Chinese food? What's the best way to pair dishes? And what's up with the naming system? From the internal cultivation of qi to the harmony between body and mind, Wudang martial arts are more than just physical training - they are a way of life rooted in the Tao.

programme.title: China Bound: Chongqing
programme.desc: Join us in southwest China's Chongqing, one of the world's biggest cities. From futuristic skylines and cyberpunk streets, to fire-breathing opera, spicy hotpot and kungfu tea, we're diving deep into this megacity the size of Austria.

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China. In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui Museum, show the amazing giant bronze mask, exquisite gold stuff, marvelous bronze divine tree etc., re-explore this mysterious and great civilization 3000 years ago.

programme.title: Crunch and Munch in Macao Ep.3
programme.desc: Feast on the stories behind Macao's iconic dishes and its people - One Country, Two Systems, endless flavors.

programme.title: Chengdu Lacquerware Art
programme.desc: Chengdu lacquerware is unique, thanks to its "three carvings and one engraving" technique. Along with its bold decorative style, this has made it a gem of Chinese lacquer art. Chengdu lacquerware also emphasizes the use of vibrant colors. Pieces are brought to beautiful life by bright red, vivid yellow, emerald green, and other striking hues.

programme.title: Discovering the Ancient Grottoes of Chongqing
programme.desc: The third episode of the Chongqing Series, Humanistic Chongqing, focuses on the Dazu Stone Carvings in Chongqing. In 1999, the Dazu Stone Carvings were inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List. As an outstanding representative of China's late grotto carving art, they integrate the essence of Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism in their content, fully embodying the beauty of cultural integration. This episode comprehensively showcases the profound historical and cultural heritage of Dazu and its vibrant contemporary folk customs, exploring the thematic connotations, artistic characteristics and historical origins of the Dazu Stone Carvings, as well as their far-reaching influence on the local people for generations.

programme.title: China's Extraordinary Hotels 3 - Living Large
programme.desc: The third episode of the China's Extraordinary Hotels Series introduces three domestic high-end hotels with each private brand: 1. Diaoyutai Hotel Hangzhou; 2. HuaQing Palace Hotel and Spa Xi'an; 3. Songtsam Linka Shangri-la Hotel. It highlights not only the hotels' surroundings, architectural styles and interior furnishings, but also their exclusive brand visions and management philosophies.

programme.title: Hanggai brings Inner Mongolian grasslands to New York
programme.desc: You don't need to speak the language to be captivated by Hanggai's music. This Chinese folk-rock band blends powerful vocals, traditional instruments and rock energy into a sound all its own. This summer, Hanggai returns to Lincoln center, bringing the beautiful melodies of the Inner Mongolian Steppe to New York. The band members share their expectations, and the stories behind their music.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programme.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan's four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programme.title: Colors of the Daliang Mountains
programme.desc: In the first episode of our Sichuan Daliang Mountains series, we journey to Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan Province. Setting off from Xichang, the prefectural capital, we first explore Lizhou Ancient Town, the southern gateway of the Southern Silk Road. We then travel to Huili County in the southernmost part of the Daliang Mountains, where we listen to the morning bells and evening drums, try our hand at making green pottery, and pick fresh pomegranates. Finally, we head to the western part of the Greater Liangshan Mountains and step into the mysterious Lugu Lake. We visit a Mosuo family to learn about their unique culture and take part in one of the Mosuo people's most important rituals: the coming of age ceremony.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker's Guide to China: Mount Siguniang
programme.desc: In this episode, Host Tianran He is on a mission: To reach the summit of Mount Siguniang, a towering snowcapped mountain in southwestern China. Together with his friend Ma Chunlin, a photographer for National Geographic, they trek through one of China's most beautiful and biodiverse hiking routes, before making for base camp. But with worsening weather conditions and severe altitude sickness, the odds are stacked against them. Ten years ago, Tianran failed his attempt at climbing Mount Siguniang's First Peak - this time, he's all in.

programme.title: Enchanting Xiamen Ep.1: Old Gems
programme.desc: Xiamen, a key starting point of China's ancient Maritime Silk Road, is one of China's most livable cities. In this episode, host Min-Zhui Lee and co-host Pan William, an honorary citizen of Xiamen and a professor, take you on an immersive journey through the city. Explore Xiamen University, renowned as China's most beautiful university campus, and visit Wanshi Park, known as "China's First Lawn". Trace Xiamen's history through its streets, admiring the arcades that tell the stories of the city's early commercial development. Finally, board a boat to Gulangyu Islet, the "Island of Music" - the birthplace of modern music education in China, and a living "World Architecture Museum". Every corner of this islet lets you experience the past and present of Xiamen's vibrant life.

programme.title: Crunch and Munch in Macao Ep.4
programme.desc: Feast on the stories behind Macao's iconic dishes and its people - One Country, Two Systems, endless flavors.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.1
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Life in Camel Town
programme.desc: When it comes to Mongolian, most people will think of grasslands, horse racing. In fact, the camel is the king of five livestock of nomadic people. Camel is the meritorious figure in the vast desert on the Silk Road. In this episode, we go to Alashan: Camel Town in China, to experience the life of Mongolian people and camels in desert. Milking, delivering milk and collecting camels, also has a thrilling journey to pick up the newborn baby camel. We deeply feel the profound feeling between the camel raiser and their camels.

programme.title: Dance of Heroes
programme.desc: In this episode, our host "Uncle Hanzi" travels to Chaonan in Shantou to explore the story of a family devoted to the tradition of Yingge dance. Centered around inheritor Hong Shaohua, the story unfolds through his father's dedication, his daughter's passion, and his apprentices'enthusiasm - showcasing how this centuries - old folk art continues to thrive in the modern world.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.4
programme.desc: Shaanxi, almost right in the middle of China, is a true land of contrasts. South of the Qinling Mountains that divide the province, the terrain has all the allure of south China, while north of this great dividing range lies the Guanzhong Plain and the austere and otherworldly Loess Plateau. Join us for a journey into a province that presents two equally beautiful and fascinating faces to the world!

programme.title: Chinese film director Wen Muye on food, war and longing for peace
programme.desc: Once Upon a Time in the Middle East, one of China's top-grossing films this summer, follows a Chinese restaurateur whose life is upended when war erupts around him. Ahead of its international debut this September, director Wen Muye spoke to CGTN about what inspired the film, and the message he hopes it carries beyond China.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of golden snub-nosed monkeys
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China's rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: The Elegance of Luoyang
programme.desc: Luoyang, as the eastern starting point of the Silk Road, is a city with a rich history and a tradition of cultural inclusivity. As such, it enjoys a prominent position in the heritage of the whole world. In this episode, we’ll visit White Horse Temple to learn about its fascinating international background. At Longmen Grottoes, which were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the year 2000, we’ll appreciate how the unique ancient splendor is being revived by 3D technology. At the city’s annual Peony Festival, we’ll explore the significance of China’s national flower and national dress. Invited to a Luoyang Water Banquet, we’ll learn something about the city’s culinary traditions. And finally, a master of tang sancai, or tri-color pottery, will discuss the legacy of this ancient craft and its place in the modern era.

programme.title: Razor: Traces of China Ep.3
programme.desc: Chinese elements can be found in many great European mansions, gardens and other public spaces. Join us as we look into these hidden features, motifs and designs and uncover a legacy of East-West cultural exchange that is all too often overlooked!

programme.title: General Guan Yu Ep.4
programme.desc: This documentary is a unique exploration of the late Eastern Han dynasty general Guan Yu. Through a gaming team's recreation of the Battle of Xiangfan, overseas collections of his porcelain sculptures, and a coming-of-age ceremony at Guandi temple, this episode recounts his military achievements, while describing a man of loyalty, righteousness, courage, and honor - and an enduring spiritual symbol for the Chinese people.

programme.title: Diabolo
programme.desc: In China, the diabolo has a history of over 600 years. From the earliest uniaxial design, it developed to have a double axis. With time, it came to be made in various shapes and from various materials. And its popularity began to spread around the world. In the hands of an expert, a diabolo can create a truly mesmerizing spectacle. So, let's hear from a professional about the various tricks of his trade.

programme.desc: Stay tuned as Deutsche Welle (DW), Germany's international broadcaster presents the country’s news, current affairs and showcases its people's life and mentality.

programme.title: DocFilm
programme.sub-title: Weapon of War - Sexual Violence Against Men
programme.desc: Sexual violence is a well-known weapon of war. One that is deployed against men, as well as women. The enemy is not killed, but destroyed nonetheless. In this documentary, men from Ukraine, Congo and Bosnia break their silence.

programme.title: DW News
programme.desc: Stay tuned as Deutsche Welle (DW), Germany's international broadcaster presents the country’s news, current affairs and showcases its people's life and mentality.

programme.title: The Day
programme.desc: Stay tuned as Deutsche Welle (DW), Germany's international broadcaster presents the country’s news, current affairs and showcases its people's life and mentality.

programme.title: The Dip
programme.desc: The Dip is a weekly business and economics podcast from Deutsche Welle that connects the dots on global money, power, and geopolitical consequences. Hosted by DW, the show delves into major issues like Europe's digital sovereignty, critical supply chains, and the shift in the continent's industrial and defense sectors.

programme.title: Angkor: The Lost Empire of Cambodia
programme.desc: At the height of its power between the 9th and 15th centuries, Angkor was a resplendent city, considered the most extensive urban complex of the pre-industrial world. But by the late 16th century, the empire was in its death throes. The people of Angkor left not a single word explaining their kingdom's collapse. Come along this giant screen adventure to unveil the mysteries behind this lost jewel of Cambodia!

programme.title: Last Devils
programme.desc: Tasmanian Devils are the world's largest carnivorous marsupials and they are only found in Tasmania. Through hundreds of hours of filming in the wild, we reveal how fights over food are a carefully choreographed ritual, we witness the seemingly brutal mating process, see tiny young developing inside their mother's pouch, and visit wild devil pups play-fighting and hunting as they prepare for life in the outside world.

programme.title: Destination Myanmar
programme.desc: Myanmar, also known as Burma. The Land of thousands of Golden Pagodas. Scattered like pearls around the country side. A country with some of the most beautiful scenery in Asia. Its culture and wildlife wrapped in mystique. A globally recognized biodiversity hotspot with unbroken habitats that harbor many endangered species, depicted in this tv-program ... such as the Dusky Leaf Monkey, Wild Asian Elephant, the Tapir, the Stump Tailed Macaques.

programme.title: Japan: The Sense of Season
programme.desc: In this episode, we delve into the spring and summer months. Spring is a time of fleeting beauty as Japan’s famous cherry blossom drifts across the nation and wild visitors welcome the warming conditions. As spring rolls into summer, dramatic festivals, mysterious animals and seasonal harvests spark into life right across Japan’s islands and coastal waters.

programme.title: End of the Big Cats
programme.desc: Leopards are more resistant to extinction because of their elusive behaviour. Leopards are solitary creatures, the quintessential ambush-and-stalking predator, able to find the most remotes places on earth to avoid human contact. This gives it a better chance of survival than lions and cheetah.

programme.title: End of the Big Cats
programme.desc: Cheetahs have already survived one extinction, estimated to have been around 10,000 years ago. Now, seen as a pest by farmers, and hunted vigorously, the cheetah is perilously close to a second exit.

programme.title: End of the Big Cats
programme.desc: This final episode recaps our discoveries so far, and traces the disastrous journey into near- extinction for the Big Cats. Finally, we ask the question: can the cats be saved? And what needs to be done?

programme.title: Wildest Indochina
programme.desc: Malaysia is one of a handful of countries in the world described as mega-diverse. Rivers and streams carve up the forests, drawing pygmy elephants to their grassy banks. Water trickles down through Malaysia’s soft bedrock excavating vast caves where bats and cockroaches thrive in their millions. Malaysia’s animals and plants have exploited every opportunity to carve out an existence and so have adapted to some very strange ways of life.

programme.title: Wildest Indochina
programme.desc: Thailand is a land of extremes. A country shaped by wild forces, where animals face tough challenges to survive. Forming part of a biodiversity hotspot Thailand encompasses a diverse range of habitats: tropical rainforest older than the Amazon and primeval caves; mangrove swamps and rocky shorelines. Inevitably, the creatures are remarkable too.

programme.title: Wildest Indochina
programme.desc: Cambodia is one of the most bio diverse countries in southeast Asia, whose wildlife and climate is ruled by the monsoon cycle. It is a wild land of extreme rains, raging rivers and flooding lakes that create great challenges for its animals, and a fine balance between seasons. The monsoon it helps reshape environments and even changes the course of a river.

programme.title: African Nostalgia
programme.desc: Africa seen and described through the eyes of a wildlife photographer who has always been fascinated by the unique atmosphere of this extraordinary continent.

programme.title: Inhabit: A permaculture Perspective
programme.desc: Inhabit: A Permaculture Perspective explores the many environmental issues facing us today and examines solutions that are being applied using the ecological design process called "permaculture"; a design method and philosophy of life with great potential for solving issues related to agriculture, economics and governance. 'Inhabit' provides an intimate look at permaculture peoples and practices ranging from rural, suburban and urban landscapes. This beautifully made documentary presents a vast array of projects, concepts and translates the diversity of permaculture into something that can be understood by an equally diverse audience. For those familiar, it will be a call to action and a glimpse into what's possible. For those unfamiliar, it will be an introduction to a new way of being and a new way of relating to the Earth. For everyone, it will be a reminder that humans are capable of being planetary healing forces. Audience Favorite Princeton Environmental Film Festival 2015. Audience Choice Award EFFY Environmental Film Festival Yale 2015. Official Selections 2015: Food + Farm Film Fest SF, G2 Green Earth Film Festival, FICMA, Life Sciences Film Festival Prague, American Conservation Film Festival, Finger Lakes Environmental Film Festival, ITSA Back to Nature Film Festival & Crossroads Festival for Documentary Film and Discourse.

programme.title: Predator's Playground
programme.desc: This African spring is a lifeline and a trap. Flowing from a sandy riverbed 30 km from the Zambezi, it draws animals from August to November. But cliffs turn it into an ambush zone for lion prides, who strike with deadly precision, taking prey from buffalo to baby elephants. It’s a predator’s playground.

programme.title: Life On Fire
programme.desc: In 2010, the eruption of the Eyjafjallajokull volcano in Iceland provoked a vast economic chaos by paralysing one of the world's major air traffic networks for several days. Through spectacular aerial footage, the film tries to understand which volcano could wake up next and what the consequences of a major eruption are likely to be. The world has come to realize that a colossal power sleeps beneath Iceland but Icelanders have learned to live amongst their volcanoes for centuries.

programme.title: Life On Fire
programme.desc: Whether the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Colombia, Chile, Italy, or Iceland, each of these countries is home to active volcanoes that are a threat to the populations settled at their feet. To avoid disasters, volcanologists are asked to anticipate and warn, they are asked to be prophets and to know how to analyze the volcanoes' slightest tremors. Around the world, these volcano doctors use their tools and knowledge to try and protect those who live in the path of the Earth's fire.

programme.title: Life On Fire
programme.desc: In Alaska, the fresh water that feeds the rivers is snowmelt from North America's highest mountains and most active volcanoes. Time and again, they erupt and poison the rivers. Scientists have only just begun to piece together what might have happened nearly 2,000 years ago, when one race of salmon faced the death of their natal river and were forced back to the open ocean - on an extraordinary adventure ...

programme.title: Ten Deadliest Snakes with Nigel Marven
programme.desc: Costa Rica has two venomous snakes for every hectare of land, including some of the world's most feared tropical snakes. Which of these kings of the jungle will make it to the top of Nigel's list?

programme.title: Ten Deadliest Snakes with Nigel Marven
programme.desc: The USA is the land of the rattlesnake – there are over 30 species of rattler found here. But what's the deadliest serpent in the country?

programme.title: Ten Deadliest Snakes with Nigel Marven
programme.desc: With almost 2000 snakebites causing 250 deaths every year, South Africa is a hotspot for deadly snakes, with some of the most feared serpents in the world. But what's the most deadly?

programme.title: Sharks, Scavengers of the Seas
programme.desc: Before being an earthly paradise with enchanting colours, the lagoon of New Caledonia is above all a paradise for sharks. But not just any sharks: they are used to being considered as fearsome predators, they are essentially opportunistic scavengers. After the flood of documentaries and fictions describing sharks as formidable predators, this film, shot over four years, intends to restore the sharks' reputation and to put them back in their true scavenger roles, which are essential to the balance of the marine ecosystem.

programme.title: Strange Creatures of the Batangas Sea
programme.desc: Hidden in the magical underwater world of one of the most biodiverse marine areas on the planet exists a community of spectacular animals more peculiar than we can imagine.

programme.title: Giants of Fortune - The Whale Sharks of Oslob
programme.desc: In the little Filipino village of Oslob on the Cebu Island, people suffer from typhoons and overfishing. Until the world's biggest fish and the Internet change everything.

programme.title: The Best of Worlds: Life at Its Alpine Limits
programme.desc: For 5000 years man has sought to inhabit the more accessible areas of Europe, but at its very heart, in the high zones of the Alps, there exists a world parallel to ours.

programme.desc: Africa seen and described through the eyes of a wildlife photographer who has always been fascinated by the unique atmosphere of this extraordinary continent.

programme.title: The New Frontier S3
programme.desc: Sondes door het zonnestelsel sturen is de droom van een wiskundige, maar de nachtmerrie van een ingenieur. Sondes worden rond een baan om planeten geslingerd om naar hun bestemming te komen. Wij volgen de nieuwste sondes die op het punt staan om door het zonnestelsel te slingeren.

programme.title: The New Frontier S3
programme.desc: Door constante observatie vanuit een baan om de Aarde hebben wetenschappers in de loop van de tijd veel data verzameld over hoe de Aarde ademt en het leven zich hier in stand kan houden.

programme.title: The New Frontier S3
programme.desc: Kosmische straling en röntgenstralen: deze mysterieuze en zeer krachtige deeltjes uit de diepe ruimte worden geanalyseerd om te ontdekken waar ze vandaan komen.

programme.title: The New Frontier S3
programme.desc: De LISA pathfinder heeft het mogelijk gemaakt om zwaartekrachtgolfdetectors in de ruimte te krijgen. Wat zijn zwaartekrachtgolven precies en waarom zijn ze zo moeilijk te detecteren?

programme.title: The New Frontier S3
programme.desc: De ionosfeer, waar de Aarde in contact komt met de ruimte, wordt slecht begrepen. Het beïnvloedt radiocommunicatie, GPS-signalen en satellieten; het verandert van dag tot nacht en het wordt beïnvloed vanuit de ruimte en door de Aarde. Nieuwe satellieten zijn gelanceerd om deze zone te bestuderen.

programme.title: How the Universe Works S2
programme.desc: Water-rich asteroids and metal space rocks shaped planetary history and hold clues to the origin of life.

programme.title: How the Universe Works S2
programme.desc: Cataclysmic cosmic blasts shaped Earth's formation, raising questions about whether similar worlds exist elsewhere.

programme.title: Supersonic: The Great Adventure
programme.desc: The epic story of 70 years of supersonic innovation, from Chuck Yeager's breakthrough to the future of flight.

programme.title: Made in Britain S1
programme.sub-title: Ambrosia's desserts and Young's battered fish
programme.desc: Om te ontdekken hoe zijn favoriete maaltijd — fish & chips gevolgd door rijstpudding — wordt gemaakt, bezoekt Lord Prescott de Ambrosia-fabriek in Devon om het productieproces van klassieke Britse desserts te verkennen. Daarna reist hij terug naar het noorden, naar Grimsby, waar hij bij de Young’s-fabriek leert hoe hun beroemde vispastei wordt gemaakt.

programme.title: Made in Britain S1
programme.desc: Op zoek naar de ultieme Britse combinatie — thee en biscuits — reist Lord Prescott naar Liverpool, waar hij de Typhoo-theefabriek bezoekt en ontdekt wat er nodig is voor een perfect gezet kopje thee. Terug in Yorkshire stopt hij bij de Fox’s-biscuitsfabriek, waarmee hij zijn reis afsluit met een echte Britse traktatie.

programme.title: Made in Britain S1
programme.desc: Op een nostalgische reis om twee van zijn jeugdfavorieten te herontdekken bezoekt Lord Prescott de Ribena-fabriek, waar hij ziet hoe de iconische zwartebessensiroop wordt gemaakt — met 90% van de zwartebessen uit het VK. In Herefordshire bezoekt hij vervolgens de Tyrrells-fabriek en ontdekt hij hoe een kleinschalig landbouwbedrijf zijn eigen aardappelen verwerkt tot ambachtelijke chips.

programme.title: Rethink S1

programme.title: Rethink S1

programme.title: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S1
programme.desc: Een moordenaar probeert zijn laatste slachtoffer te vermoorden terwijl de auto waar zij in zitten naar de bodem van een meer zinkt. De enige manier om het slachtoffer te redden is om haar te redden terwijl de auto zinkt. Wij testen meerdere handpistolen onder water om te zien of je er echt het raam van een auto mee kunt breken om het slachtoffer te redden.

programme.title: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S1
programme.desc: In deze iconische scène hangt Chief Brody aan een zinkende boot terwijl een enorme haai hem nadert met een zuurstoffles in de bek. We bouwen een enorme haai op een motorplatform om te testen of je de fles kunt raken en laten exploderen met een jachtgeweer terwijl je je in een precaire situatie bevindt.

programme.title: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S1

programme.title: Key & Peele
programme.desc: Jordan og Keegan har en flickerkamp og en MMA-fighter går for vidt, når han disser modstanderen. Andre sketches inkluderer en bryllupsgæst, der vil være dj og spille 'klassiske' numre.

programme.title: Key & Peele: Sexy Vampires

programme.title: Key & Peele: Slap-Ass
programme.desc: Sketches inkluderer at fyrene har en dårlig Skype-forbindelse, en Django Unchained-slavekamp og en baseballspiller, der klasker røv for meget.

programme.title: Key & Peele: Airplane Showdown

programme.title: Key & Peele: Les Miz

programme.desc: Two hapless soldiers of misfortune (Chuck Norris, Louis Gossett Jr.) meet a beautiful girl (Melody Anderson) with a map to a lost gold mine and decide to have one last shot at striking it rich. But the trail to the treasure is no yellow brick road!

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: 6 June 1944: D-Day. In the early hours of 6 June 1944, the invasion of France begins. A million-and-a-half men take part. It is the bloodiest day in American history since the Civil War, though the Allies succeed in tearing a 45-mile gap in Hitler's vaunted Atlantic Wall. By day's end more than 150,000 men have landed on French soil, and more men, equipment and supplies are coming ashore every hour. A series by Ken Burns. Part 7 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: June 1944 to August 1944. American and British troops in Normandy are bogged down in the hedgerows, while in the Pacific, the marines fight their costliest battle to date on the island of Saipan. Back home, dreaded telegrams from the War Department begin arriving at a rate inconceivable just one year earlier. But by mid-August, the Germans are in full retreat out of France, and on 25 August, after four years of Nazi occupation, Paris is liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 8 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In September of 1944, with their troops in Europe stalled on the German border having outrun their supply lines, Allied commanders gamble on a risky plan to drop thousands of airborne troops behind enemy lines in Holland. When the mission ends in disaster, it becomes painfully clear that the war in Europe will not end before winter. In the Pacific, on the island of Peleliu, the marines fight one of the most brutal campaigns of the war. A series by Ken Burns. Part 9 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In the late autumn of 1944 American soldiers suffer terrible losses when they are ordered into the forbidding and fiercely defended terrain of the Hrtgen Forest and the Vosges Mountains. In the Central Pacific, to the delight of audiences back home, General MacArthur returns to the island of Leyte. But months of bloody fighting lie ahead before the Philippine Islands, and the people imprisoned on them, can be liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 10 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Winter 1944 to 1945. The Allies are unprepared for Hitler's counterattack in the Ardennes Forest of Belgium and Luxembourg. It is the biggest battle of the war on the Western Front, fought during the coldest winter in memory. By the time the Battle of the Bulge is over, Hitler's enormous gamble has ended in disaster and the Russians are approaching Berlin. Meanwhile, in the Santo Tomas Camp in the Philippines, thousands of internees await liberation. A series by Ken Burns. Part 11 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Winter to Spring 1945. On the island of Iwo Jima, the marines face 21,000 Japanese defenders who, without hope of reinforcement, have been ordered to kill as many Americans as possible before being killed themselves. Once the island is taken, Allied bombers set the cities of Japan ablaze, killing thousands and leaving millions homeless. In Europe, Americans are crossing the Rhine and driving into Germany, while the Russians are within 50 miles of Berlin. A series by Ken Burns. Part 12 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Spring 1945. In the Pacific, Americans fight on the island of Okinawa while kamikaze pilots wreak havoc on the fleet offshore. In Europe, allied forces rapidly push across Germany from the east and west, and American and British troops discover the true horrors of the Nazis' industrialised barbarism at Buchenwald, Dachau, Mauthausen and other concentration camps. Finally, on 8 May, with their country in ruins and their Fuhrer dead, the Germans surrender. A series by Ken Burns. Part 13 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: May to December 1945. In June, the battle on Okinawa ends yet Japan's rulers, despite the agony their people are enduring, resist unconditional surrender. On 6 August 1945, an American plane drops an atomic bomb on Hiroshima. Two days later, Russia declares war against Japan. A second atomic bomb is dropped on Nagasaki and, finally, Japan surrenders. In the following months, hundreds of thousands of American servicemen and women return home. A series by Ken Burns. Part 14 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: December 1941 to March 1942. The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941 thrusts the United States into the global cataclysm that will eventually touch every family on every street in every town in America. Within a few months, millions of young men have entered the armed forces and are beginning to train for war. A series by Ken Burns. Part 1 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: March 1942 to December 1942. With U-boats menacing the East Coast, and little good news from overseas, many worry that the United States is utterly unprepared to fight in a 'total war'. But after six months of gruelling combat on Guadalcanal, the Americans finally stop Japan's expansion in the Pacific. A series by Ken Burns. Part 2 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: January 1943 to June 1943. American troops land in North Africa and test themselves for the first time against the German and Italian armies, learning to set aside the notion that killing is a sin, and adopting the outlook that 'killing is a craft'. Back home, cities become booming 'war towns' overnight as nearly all manufacturing is converted to the war effort, and thousands of women become industrial workers. A series by Ken Burns. Part 3 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: July 1943 to December 1943. On daylight bombing missions, American airmen gamble with their lives against overwhelming odds to bring the war to the heart of Hitler's vast empire. Allied forces invade Sicily and then Italy but, as they grind their way towards Rome, the weather turns bad and the terrain grows more and more forbidding. Twisting mountain roads and blown bridges have to be negotiated while under constant German fire. A series by Ken Burns. Part 4 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: November 1943 to February 1944. In November, the US marines take the tiny Pacific atoll of Tarawa, but at a terrible cost. Back home, Japanese-Americans are permitted to form a special segregated infantry unit and begin to train for combat. As the war economy booms, ugly racial violence erupts in cities across the country. Overseas, in the mountains south of Rome, the allies try to fight their way around the edges of Monte Cassino, but are stopped cold. A series by Ken Burns. Part 5 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: January 1944 to June 1944. American and British troops are pinned down at Anzio for months, while at Monte Cassino, the killing goes on and on. African-Americans, incensed at the segregation of the armed forces, put pressure on the military to make some changes. In May, allied soldiers at Cassino and Anzio resume their drive northward in Italy, liberating Rome on 4 June, but they let the retreating German army get away. A series by Ken Burns. Part 6 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: 6 June 1944: D-Day. In the early hours of 6 June 1944, the invasion of France begins. A million-and-a-half men take part. It is the bloodiest day in American history since the Civil War, though the Allies succeed in tearing a 45-mile gap in Hitler's vaunted Atlantic Wall. By day's end more than 150,000 men have landed on French soil, and more men, equipment and supplies are coming ashore every hour. A series by Ken Burns. Part 7 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: June 1944 to August 1944. American and British troops in Normandy are bogged down in the hedgerows, while in the Pacific, the marines fight their costliest battle to date on the island of Saipan. Back home, dreaded telegrams from the War Department begin arriving at a rate inconceivable just one year earlier. But by mid-August, the Germans are in full retreat out of France, and on 25 August, after four years of Nazi occupation, Paris is liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 8 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In September of 1944, with their troops in Europe stalled on the German border having outrun their supply lines, Allied commanders gamble on a risky plan to drop thousands of airborne troops behind enemy lines in Holland. When the mission ends in disaster, it becomes painfully clear that the war in Europe will not end before winter. In the Pacific, on the island of Peleliu, the marines fight one of the most brutal campaigns of the war. A series by Ken Burns. Part 9 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In the late autumn of 1944 American soldiers suffer terrible losses when they are ordered into the forbidding and fiercely defended terrain of the Hrtgen Forest and the Vosges Mountains. In the Central Pacific, to the delight of audiences back home, General MacArthur returns to the island of Leyte. But months of bloody fighting lie ahead before the Philippine Islands, and the people imprisoned on them, can be liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 10 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Winter 1944 to 1945. The Allies are unprepared for Hitler's counterattack in the Ardennes Forest of Belgium and Luxembourg. It is the biggest battle of the war on the Western Front, fought during the coldest winter in memory. By the time the Battle of the Bulge is over, Hitler's enormous gamble has ended in disaster and the Russians are approaching Berlin. Meanwhile, in the Santo Tomas Camp in the Philippines, thousands of internees await liberation. A series by Ken Burns. Part 11 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Winter to Spring 1945. On the island of Iwo Jima, the marines face 21,000 Japanese defenders who, without hope of reinforcement, have been ordered to kill as many Americans as possible before being killed themselves. Once the island is taken, Allied bombers set the cities of Japan ablaze, killing thousands and leaving millions homeless. In Europe, Americans are crossing the Rhine and driving into Germany, while the Russians are within 50 miles of Berlin. A series by Ken Burns. Part 12 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Spring 1945. In the Pacific, Americans fight on the island of Okinawa while kamikaze pilots wreak havoc on the fleet offshore. In Europe, allied forces rapidly push across Germany from the east and west, and American and British troops discover the true horrors of the Nazis' industrialised barbarism at Buchenwald, Dachau, Mauthausen and other concentration camps. Finally, on 8 May, with their country in ruins and their Fuhrer dead, the Germans surrender. A series by Ken Burns. Part 13 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: May to December 1945. In June, the battle on Okinawa ends yet Japan's rulers, despite the agony their people are enduring, resist unconditional surrender. On 6 August 1945, an American plane drops an atomic bomb on Hiroshima. Two days later, Russia declares war against Japan. A second atomic bomb is dropped on Nagasaki and, finally, Japan surrenders. In the following months, hundreds of thousands of American servicemen and women return home. A series by Ken Burns. Part 14 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: December 1941 to March 1942. The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941 thrusts the United States into the global cataclysm that will eventually touch every family on every street in every town in America. Within a few months, millions of young men have entered the armed forces and are beginning to train for war. A series by Ken Burns. Part 1 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: March 1942 to December 1942. With U-boats menacing the East Coast, and little good news from overseas, many worry that the United States is utterly unprepared to fight in a 'total war'. But after six months of gruelling combat on Guadalcanal, the Americans finally stop Japan's expansion in the Pacific. A series by Ken Burns. Part 2 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: January 1943 to June 1943. American troops land in North Africa and test themselves for the first time against the German and Italian armies, learning to set aside the notion that killing is a sin, and adopting the outlook that 'killing is a craft'. Back home, cities become booming 'war towns' overnight as nearly all manufacturing is converted to the war effort, and thousands of women become industrial workers. A series by Ken Burns. Part 3 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: January 1943 to June 1943. American troops land in North Africa and test themselves for the first time against the German and Italian armies, learning to set aside the notion that killing is a sin, and adopting the outlook that 'killing is a craft'. Back home, cities become booming 'war towns' overnight as nearly all manufacturing is converted to the war effort, and thousands of women become industrial workers. A series by Ken Burns. Part 3 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: July 1943 to December 1943. On daylight bombing missions, American airmen gamble with their lives against overwhelming odds to bring the war to the heart of Hitler's vast empire. Allied forces invade Sicily and then Italy but, as they grind their way towards Rome, the weather turns bad and the terrain grows more and more forbidding. Twisting mountain roads and blown bridges have to be negotiated while under constant German fire. A series by Ken Burns. Part 4 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: November 1943 to February 1944. In November, the US marines take the tiny Pacific atoll of Tarawa, but at a terrible cost. Back home, Japanese-Americans are permitted to form a special segregated infantry unit and begin to train for combat. As the war economy booms, ugly racial violence erupts in cities across the country. Overseas, in the mountains south of Rome, the allies try to fight their way around the edges of Monte Cassino, but are stopped cold. A series by Ken Burns. Part 5 of 14.

programme.title: The War

programme.title: Destruction Decoded: TORNADO
programme.desc: A tornado is a violently rotating column of air extending from the base of a thunderstorm down to the ground. Tornadoes are capable of completely destroying well-made structures, uprooting trees, and hurling objects through the air like deadly missiles.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded: EARTHQUAKES
programme.desc: Earthquakes happen when tectonic plates suddenly slip causing shock waves to shake the surface of the Earth. They occur on fault lines - the most active are the Ring of Fire in the Pacific Ocean and the San Andreas fault on America’s west coast.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded: VOLCANOES
programme.desc: Volcanoes are Earth’s geologic architects. They’ve created more than 80 percent of our planet’s surface and their explosive force has crafted both mountains and craters.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded: MEGAFLOODS
programme.desc: Water covers two thirds of the earth’s surface, and we are utterly dependent on it, but when this vital ingredient of life unleashes its fury on the planet it becomes the ultimate bringer of death.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Dronino, Russia
programme.desc: The Kremlin, St. Basil's Cathedral, the Red Square, and of course, shots of vodka... for the first time, Geoff and Steve make the journey to Russia in search of one of the most rare and valuable meteorites on the planet—the Dronino ataxite.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Brenham, Kansas
programme.desc: In Brenham, Kansas pieces of a large meteorite that fell thousands of years ago have been unearthed. Using advanced metal detection equipment Arnold and Notkin work tirelessly to find the meteorite pieces that have yet to be discovered.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Return to Whitecourt
programme.desc: An important scientific mission summons the Meteorite Men back to Canada.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Kansas: Return To Alpha
programme.desc: Geoff and Steve return to their confidential "Alpha" site. During a research and development visit to Orange County Choppers, they help plan a meteorite hunting motorcycle, which is delivered to them by American Chopper star Paul Senior.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Gold Basin
programme.desc: In 1995, Professor Jim Kriegh discovered a field of of ancient stone meteorites; the Gold Basin Meteorite is known as the best mapped strewn field in history. In this episode, Geoff and Steve get exclusive access to hunt meteorites in uncharted areas.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Morasko, Poland
programme.desc: 5,000 years ago, an enormous meteorite cascaded over Poland scarring the landscape with seven massive craters. For the first time, Geoff and Steve receive exclusive access to investigate the magnificent Morasko crater field.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Australia 1: Henbury Craters
programme.desc: In the Season Two finale Geoff and Steve journey to one of the most remarkable meteorite sites on the planet—the Henbury Crater field in central Australia.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Australia 2: Mundrabilla
programme.desc: Steve and Geoff head on an ambitious expedition. On the far side of the world, they cross the Nullarbor Plainand reach the remote Mundrabilla strewnfield. They team up with Australian meteorite specialist Dr. Andy Tomkins.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: The Tucson Ring
programme.desc: In the 1850s a farmer came across a meteorite in Arizona; it's known as the "Tucson Ring" and now resides at the Smithsonian. Arnold and Notkin search for more pieces in an attempt to solve one of the biggest mysteries in the world of meteorite hunters.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Return to Sweden
programme.desc: On this episode, Geoff and Steve make their epic return to northern Sweden in order to reclaim victory north of the Arctic Circle.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Chile 1: Imilac & Vaca Muerta
programme.desc: In the first-ever overseas Meteorite Men episode Steve and Geoff revisit the very site where their hunting partnership began way back in 1997: the Imilac pallasite strewnfield high in Chile's Atacama Desert.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Chile 2: Monturaqui Crater & San Juan
programme.desc: Geoff's "meteorite dream" comes true during this second Chile episode when the guys find their way to the Atacama Desert's remote Monturaqui Crater, and camp overnight on the floor of the stunning 100,000 year-old impact site.

programme.title: Meteorite Men: Wisconsin Fireball
